prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Quickbase in an empty repository. Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Tailwind CSS; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records in a constrained operational database for one small team, provide form, grid, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command using Docker Compose for the database.
Store all user data locally by default and make data export straightforward. Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a schema builder UI that allows users to create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views dynamically without writing code.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, basic formulas, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema, allowing users to switch seamlessly between them.
Add role-based permissions (admin, editor, viewer), optimistic concurrency checks, audit history tracking for record changes, and a trash restore feature.
Provide CSV import and export functionality, and auto-generate a token-authenticated REST API based on the user's defined schema.
Ship database migrations, seed data, health checks, and a schema export format. Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states across the UI.
Add strict input validation, safe filename handling for attachments, and graceful error handling.
Write focused tests for the core data transformation logic and one end-to-end happy path for creating a record.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane. Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility, hundreds of enterprise integrations, and large-enterprise governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
